prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Miami after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first, a quick clarification so I give the best matches:

- Do you want a large/national firm or a smaller local/boutique trial firm?  
- Do you need Spanish-speaking counsel?  
- Was anyone seriously injured (hospitalized, surgery, permanent disability) or is this a lower‑severity crash?

If you want names now, here are several reputable firms with a Miami presence to call and why each is worth contacting. I can pull phone numbers/addresses if you want.

1) Morgan & Morgan (Miami)  
Why call: One of the largest plaintiff firms in the U.S. with substantial resources to handle insurance companies, full-time investigators and medical staff, and experience with high-volume car accident and catastrophic-injury cases. Good if you want a firm that can scale to handle complex medical bills, lost wages and litigation.

2) Colson Hicks Eidson (Miami)  
Why call: Well-known Florida plaintiff boutique that focuses on serious personal-injury and wrongful-death cases, with trial experience and a reputation for handling catastrophic injuries. Good if you want a firm with local trial experience and a track record in high-stakes cases.

3) Anidjar & Levine (Florida, with Miami-area presence)  
Why call: Florida personal injury firm that focuses on auto accidents, slip-and-fall and wrongful death. Often handles many car-accident claims and offers free consultations; useful for straightforward and moderate-severity claims.

4) Steinger, Greene & Feiner (offices in Florida including Miami area)  
Why call: Florida-based personal injury firm experienced with auto collisions and DUI/serious injury cases. They advertise contingency-fee representation and often emphasize client communication and case management.

Why I recommend calling several different firms
- Different firms have different strengths (trial experience, medical resources, negotiation skill, bilingual staff).  
- Some firms are better at catastrophic claims; others are set up for quick, fair settlements for moderate injuries.  
- Comparing a few gives you leverage and helps you choose the fee structure and communication style you prefer.

What to ask when you call (5–7 quick questions)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases in Miami County? How many car-accident cases did you handle last year?  
- Do you take cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover)? What percentage and what costs will be deducted?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)? Will I have that person’s direct number?  
- Do you have experience trying cases to verdict in Miami-Dade courts? Any recent outcomes you can share (no promises — just examples)?  
- Do you handle communications with insurance companies and medical liens?  
- Do you have Spanish-speaking staff (if needed)?  
- How soon should I expect a case strategy and next steps?

Documents to have ready for the call
- Police report number (if available), date/time and location of crash  
- Photos of damage/injuries, medical records or bills, and contact info of witnesses  
- Insurance information (your policy and the other driver’s)  
- Any employer/HR notes about missed work

Red flags to watch for
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount or promise of results — no lawyer can guarantee a result.  
- High up-front fees (most reputable PI lawyers handle on contingency).  
- Poor communication during the initial call.

Next step
Tell me your preferences (large vs boutique, Spanish required, severity of injury) and I’ll give a tailored list of 4–6 Miami firms with phone numbers and a recommended first call to make. Also, if you want, I can prepare a short phone script you can read during calls.
